mainTopic: From whom did רבי עקיבא learn the cucumber כישוף? The story of רבי אליעזר's death, and the rule that כישוף may be learned in order to understand and teach.
overview: Just before this, the גמרא said that רבי עקיבא learned the laws of כישוף, such as making cucumbers appear, from רבי יהושע. Now it challenges this with a long ברייתא about the death of רבי אליעזר. The sick רבי אליעזר, who was under a ban, shows his mind is clear. He rebukes the חכמים for never coming to learn from him. He mourns that so much of his תורה was never asked about, except the laws of planting cucumbers, which only רבי עקיבא asked about and saw him perform. He answers the חכמים' questions about טומאה and dies saying the word 'טהור'. רבי יהושע then lifts the ban, and רבי עקיבא mourns him bitterly. The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא first heard it from רבי אליעזר without understanding it, and only later understood it from רבי יהושע. It then asks how רבי אליעזר could perform כישוף at all, and answers that doing it in order to learn and teach is permitted. With this the פרק ארבע מיתות ends.

steps.title: Did רבי עקיבא really learn this from רבי יהושע?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the earlier claim that רבי עקיבא learned these laws from רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did רבי עקיבא really learn this from רבי יהושע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge against what it just said. It is setting up a source that will show a different teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא said רבי עקיבא learned the laws of כישוף from רבי יהושע. The word וְהָא signals that the גמרא is about to bring a source that seems to contradict this.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But did Rabbi Akiva
learn it from Rabbi Yehoshua?
phrases.notes: "It" means the laws of כישוף that the גמרא was just talking about.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מֵרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ גְּמִיר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the previous statement on the daf that רבי עקיבא learned from רבי יהושע.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי עקיבא learned the laws of כישוף from רבי יהושע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא will show that רבי עקיבא learned these laws from רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: The ברייתא begins: visiting the sick רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא and his colleagues come to visit רבי אליעזר when he is sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: When רבי אליעזר became sick, רבי עקיבא and his colleagues came to visit him. He was sitting in his canopied bed, and they were sitting in his front room.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that is the source of its challenge. It starts by setting the scene.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof itself comes at the end of the story. Right now we only learn where everyone is: רבי אליעזר is in his bed, and the visitors wait in another room.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the proof in this part of the story. It comes later, when רבי אליעזר tells the visiting חכמים that only רבי עקיבא asked him about planting cucumbers, and describes how he taught him (steps 11–12).

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
When Rabbi Eliezer became ill,
Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues came in to visit him.
He was sitting in his canopied bed,
and they were sitting in his parlor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: כְּשֶׁחָלָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the challenge in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא learned these laws from רבי אליעזר, not from רבי יהושע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the illness of רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: הורקנוס is scolded for removing his father's תפילין
steps.stepSummary: On ערב שבת, הורקנוס tries to take off his father's תפילין. רבי אליעזר scolds him, and the son tells the visitors his father has lost his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: That day was ערב שבת. His son הורקנוס came in to take off his תפילין. He scolded him, and the son left rebuked. The son said to his father's colleagues: It seems to me that Father's mind is confused.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on. רבי אליעזר's son tries to remove his תפילין before שבת, gets scolded, and thinks his father is no longer thinking clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תפילין are not worn on שבת, so the son thought he was doing the right thing. The scolding seemed to him to make no sense, so he decided his father's illness had affected his mind.

keyTerms.meaning: Became confused or unsettled (of the mind)

phrases.english: And that day was Erev Shabbat,
and his son Hyrcanus came in
to remove his tefillin.
He scolded him, and he left rebuked.
He said to them, to his colleagues:
phrases.notes: This is הורקנוס talking to his father's colleagues, the visiting חכמים.

phrases.english: It seems to me
that Father's mind has become confused.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הורקנוס thinks his father's mind is confused because he was scolded for removing his תפילין on ערב שבת.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר explains: first take care of the serious prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that his son and wife are the confused ones. They worry about a rabbinic prohibition and ignore prohibitions punishable by סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: His mind and his mother's mind are confused! How can they leave aside a prohibition punishable by סקילה and busy themselves with a rabbinic prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר defends himself. He explains that he scolded his son for having the wrong priorities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing תפילין on שבת is at most an איסור שבות, a rabbinic prohibition. Getting the house ready before שבת, so no one does a מלאכה punishable by סקילה, is far more urgent. His sharp answer shows his mind is perfectly clear.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition punishable by stoning, such as doing a מלאכה on שבת
A rabbinic prohibition connected to שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a basic principle: when time is short, take care of the more serious prohibition first.

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: Now רבי אליעזר is speaking, after overhearing his son.

phrases.english: His mind and his mother's mind are confused!
How can they leave aside a prohibition punishable by stoning
phrases.notes: He means getting things ready for שבת, like lighting candles and preparing food, before it becomes forbidden.

phrases.english: and busy themselves with a rabbinic prohibition?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: דַּעְתּוֹ וְדַעַת אִמּוֹ נִטְרְפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אליעזר answers his son's claim from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An איסור סקילה should be dealt with before an איסור שבות.

steps.title: The חכמים enter and sit four אמות away
steps.stepSummary: Once the חכמים see that רבי אליעזר's mind is clear, they come in and sit four אמות away from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the חכמים saw that his mind was settled, they came in and sat before him at a distance of four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The visitors now know רבי אליעזר can receive them, so they come in. They keep a distance of four אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His clear answer proved his mind was fine. They still stayed four אמות away because he was under a ban.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind was settled and clear

phrases.english: Once the Sages saw
that his mind was settled,
they came in and sat before him
at a distance of four cubits.
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר was in נידוי (see בבא מציעא נט:), and you may not sit within four אמות of someone in נידוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן שֶׁרָאוּ חֲכָמִים שֶׁדַּעְתּוֹ מְיוּשֶּׁבֶת עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the visitors reacted to רבי אליעזר's clear answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים enter but keep four אמות away from רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Why have you come, and why not until now?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks why they came. They say to learn תורה. He asks why they never came before, and they say they had no free time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Why have you come? They said: We came to learn תורה. He said: And why didn't you come until now? They said: We had no free time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר and his visitors talk. He is hurt that they never came to learn from him before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The visitors say they came to learn תורה, not just to visit a sick man. That makes רבי אליעזר ask why they stayed away until now, and their excuse is that they were too busy.

phrases.english: He said to them: Why have you come?
They said to him: We came to learn Torah.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: וְעַד עַכְשָׁיו לָמָּה לֹא בָּאתֶם?
phrases.english: He said to them: And until now, why didn't you come?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא הָיָה לָנוּ פְּנַאי.
phrases.english: They said to him: We didn't have free time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: לָמָּה בָּאתֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The conversation begins after the visitors sit down.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים admit they did not come to learn from רבי אליעזר earlier because they were busy.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר predicts harsh deaths, harshest for רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says he would be surprised if they died a natural death. רבי עקיבא asks about himself and is told his will be harsher.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I would be amazed if they die a natural death. רבי עקיבא said to him: What about mine? He said to him: Yours will be harsher than theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers their excuse with a frightening prediction. רבי עקיבא asks about himself and hears that his fate will be the hardest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not coming to learn from their teacher is treated as very serious. רבי עקיבא gets the harshest prediction, which hints that he above all should have come to learn from רבי אליעזר. This prepares for the later part of the story, where רבי אליעזר describes what he taught רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Their own death, meaning a natural death

phrases.english: He said to them: I would be amazed
if they die their own death.
phrases.notes: "Their own death" means a natural death. He is hinting they will die in a harsher way.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: שֶׁלִּי מַהוּ?
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him: What about mine?
He said to him: Yours will be harsher than theirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: תָּמֵיהַּ אֲנִי אִם יָמוּתוּ מִיתַת עַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אליעזר responds to their excuse from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר predicts unnatural deaths for the חכמים, and the harshest for רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatToRemember: The story so far sets up the bond between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא. The proof that רבי עקיבא learned from רבי אליעזר comes in steps 11–12.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר mourns over his two arms
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר puts his arms on his heart and says they are like two ספרי תורה being rolled up. He says he learned and taught much תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took his two arms, put them on his heart and said: Woe to you, my two arms, which are like two ספרי תורה being rolled up! I learned much תורה and I taught much תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר, close to death, mourns that his knowledge of תורה is about to leave the world. He opens with a short summary that the next lines will explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rolled-up ספר תורה can no longer be read. He compares his arms to two such scrolls because once he dies, the תורה inside him can no longer be reached. The line "I learned much, I taught much" is the heading for the next step.

phrases.english: He took his two arms
and placed them on his heart.
He said: Woe to you, my two arms,
for they are like two Torah scrolls being rolled up!
phrases.notes: A scroll that gets rolled up closes, and nobody can read it anymore. He means his תורה is about to be closed off.

phrases.english: I learned much Torah,
and I taught much Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָטַל שְׁתֵּי זְרוֹעוֹתָיו וְהִנִּיחָן עַל לִבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his harsh words to the חכמים and רבי עקיבא, רבי אליעזר turns to mourning his own lost תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר's תורה is like closed scrolls; it is leaving the world with him.

steps.title: How little he took, and how little was taken from him
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר explains: he took almost nothing from his teachers' huge wisdom, and his students took almost nothing from his.
steps.simpleTranslation: I learned much תורה, yet I did not take from my teachers even as much as a dog laps from the sea. I taught much תורה, yet my students took from me only as much as a paintbrush takes from a tube of paint.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר now explains the two halves of his summary, using two pictures to show how small a part of the תורה was passed on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dog lapping from the sea takes almost nothing from it. This shows how great his teachers were compared to what he took. A paintbrush dipped in a tube takes only a tiny bit, so most of his own תורה was never received by his students.

keyTerms.meaning: a brush (for painting or eye makeup)

phrases.english: I learned much Torah,
yet I did not take away from my teachers
phrases.notes: Literally "I did not make them less." He means he hardly took anything out of their wisdom.

phrases.english: even as much as a dog lapping from the sea.
I taught much Torah,
yet my students did not take away from me
except like a paintbrush in a tube.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַרְבֵּה תּוֹרָה לָמַדְתִּי, וְלֹא חִסַּרְתִּי מֵרַבּוֹתַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains each half of the summary given in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a tiny part of the תורה passed from his teachers to him, and from him to his students.

steps.title: Three hundred laws of a bright white mark that nobody asked about
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says he knows 300 הלכות about a בהרת עזה, and no one ever asked him about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not only that, but I teach three hundred הלכות about a very white בהרת, and no one ever asked me anything about them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives a concrete example of תורה that never got passed on: a whole area of הלכות of צרעת that no one ever asked him about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the earlier point in practice. He had a huge amount of knowledge in one narrow topic, but no student ever asked, so it will be lost with him.

keyTerms.meaning: a very bright white צרעת mark

phrases.english: Not only that, but
I teach three hundred halachos
about a bright white leprous mark,
phrases.notes: בהרת is one of the marks of צרעת described in ויקרא 13.

phrases.english: and there was no person who asked me
anything about them, ever.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁאֲנִי שׁוֹנֶה שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת הֲלָכוֹת בְּבַהֶרֶת עַזָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a concrete example of the תורה his students did not take from him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A whole area of הלכות of בהרת went unasked and unlearned.

steps.title: Laws of planting cucumbers that only עקיבא asked about
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר knows 300 (or 3,000) הלכות about planting cucumbers, and only רבי עקיבא ever asked about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not only that, but I teach three hundred הלכות (some say three thousand) about planting cucumbers, and no one ever asked me anything about them except עקיבא בן יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: A second example of unasked תורה, this time with one exception: רבי עקיבא. This sets up the story in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number is reported two ways, 300 or 3,000. Here, planting cucumbers means making them grow by a spoken word, as the next step shows. Naming רבי עקיבא as the only one who asked leads straight into the story of how he asked.

phrases.english: Not only that, but
I teach three hundred halachos,
and some say: three thousand halachos,
about planting cucumbers,
and there was no person who asked me
anything about them, ever,
except Akiva ben Yosef.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁאֲנִי שׁוֹנֶה שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת הֲלָכוֹת, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: שְׁלֹשֶׁת אֲלָפִים הֲלָכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second example of unasked תורה, now with רבי עקיבא as the one exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only רבי עקיבא asked about the הלכות of planting cucumbers.

steps.title: The story of planting and uprooting cucumbers
steps.stepSummary: While they walked together, רבי עקיבא asked to learn planting cucumbers. With one word רבי אליעזר filled the field, and with another word gathered them all to one place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he and I were walking on the road. He said: רבי, teach me about planting cucumbers. I said one word, and the whole field filled with cucumbers. He said: רבי, you taught me how to plant them, now teach me how to uproot them. I said one word, and they all gathered into one place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר tells the story of the one time someone asked him about the cucumber הלכות: רבי עקיבא, while they were walking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cucumbers appear and are gathered with just a spoken word, so this is clearly not normal farming. רבי עקיבא asks about both sides, planting and uprooting, which shows he wanted the full topic and not just half of it.

phrases.english: Once, he and I
were walking on the road.
He said to me: My teacher,
teach me about planting cucumbers.
I said one word,
and the whole field filled with cucumbers.
He said to me: My teacher,
you taught me their planting,
teach me their uprooting.
I said one word,
and they all gathered into one place.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּעַם אַחַת אֲנִי וָהוּא מְהַלְּכִין הָיִינוּ בַּדֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the story behind the exception mentioned in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא learned both the planting and the uprooting of cucumbers by a word from רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's sorrow is that huge areas of his תורה were never asked about. The cucumber story shows that רבי עקיבא was the one student who asked.

steps.title: The Sages ask about leather-covered objects
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רבי אליעזר about the טומאה of a ball, a shoemaker's last, an amulet, a pouch of pearls and a small weight.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: A ball, a shoemaker's last, an amulet, a pouch of pearls and a small weight: what is their law?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the חכמים, who came to learn, finally ask him a question of הלכה. His answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these items is covered in leather with something stuffed or held inside. The question is about their status for טומאה.

phrases.english: They said to him:
The ball and the shoemaker's last,
and the amulet and the pouch of pearls,
and a small weight: what is their law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: הַכַּדּוּר וְהָאִמּוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his speech, the חכמים do what they said they came for in step 6: they ask a question of תורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether these leather-covered objects can become טמא, and how they are purified.

steps.title: They can become impure and are purified as they are
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that these items can become טמא, and they are purified whole, as they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: They are טמאין, and they are purified as they are.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers the חכמים' question in two parts: the items can become טמא, and their purification works on them whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First he rules that these items can receive טומאה. Then he adds that they are purified as they are, meaning without opening them up.
steps.confusionAlert: "הן טמאין" here does not mean they are already impure. It means they are the kind of objects that can become טמא.

phrases.english: He said to them: They can become tamei,
and their purification is as they are.
phrases.notes: He means you can immerse them whole, without opening them up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: הֵן טְמֵאִין, וְטַהֲרָתָן בְּמָה שֶׁהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The items can become טמא, and they are purified whole, without being opened.

steps.title: The last question: a shoe still on its last
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רבי אליעזר one more question: is a shoe that is still sitting on the shoemaker's form able to become טמא?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law of a shoe that is still on the shoemaker's last?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים keep questioning רבי אליעזר about טומאה. This is their final question to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether a shoe that is still on the last counts as a finished כלי. A finished כלי can become טמא. An unfinished one cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: A shoemaker's last: the wooden foot-shaped form a shoe is made on

phrases.english: A shoe that is on a last, what is its law?
phrases.notes: The question is whether a shoe still on its form counts as a finished כלי that can become טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנְעָל שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי הָאִמּוּם, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of טומאה questions the חכמים put to רבי אליעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a shoe still on the last is a finished כלי that can become טמא.

steps.title: He answers 'pure' and passes away
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that the shoe is טהור, and his soul departs as he says the word 'pure'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: It is pure. And his soul left him in purity.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives his ruling, and that ruling is the last word he ever speaks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The halachic answer is that the shoe on the last is not yet a finished כלי, so it stays טהור. The story adds a deeper meaning: he died with the word 'טהור' on his lips.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure; not able to receive טומאה

phrases.english: He said to them: It is pure,
and his soul left him in purity.
phrases.notes: His very last word was 'טהור', so his soul left him with that word.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: הוּא טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shoe on the last is טהור, and רבי אליעזר dies saying this word.

steps.title: רבי יהושע announces the ban is lifted
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע stands up and declares twice that the vow (the ban on רבי אליעזר) is now released.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע stood on his feet and said: The vow is released, the vow is released!
steps.whatsHappening: Right after רבי אליעזר dies, רבי יהושע publicly announces that the ban the חכמים had placed on him is over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While he was alive, רבי אליעזר was under a ban, and people kept their distance from him. Now that he has died, רבי יהושע declares that the ban no longer applies. Saying it twice shows how strongly he felt it.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow; here, the ban placed on רבי אליעזר

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עַל רַגְלָיו וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua stood on his feet and said:
The vow is released, the vow is released!
phrases.notes: The 'vow' here means the ban the חכמים had put on רבי אליעזר. Now it is lifted.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמַד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עַל רַגְלָיו וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reaction to רבי אליעזר's death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With רבי אליעזר's death, the ban on him is released.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא meets the funeral in deep grief
steps.stepSummary: After שבת, רבי עקיבא meets the funeral on the road between קסרי and לוד, and he strikes himself until he bleeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: On מוצאי שבת, רבי עקיבא met the funeral between קסרי and לוד. He was striking his flesh until his blood flowed to the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to רבי עקיבא, who was not there when his teacher died. He meets the funeral on the road and mourns terribly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's extreme grief shows how much he valued רבי אליעזר. It also shows his pain at having missed learning from him during the years of the ban.

keyTerms.meaning: He met him (here, met his funeral)

phrases.english: At the conclusion of Shabbat,
Rabbi Akiva encountered him
phrases.notes: He means רבי עקיבא met the funeral procession.

phrases.english: between Caesarea and Lod.
He was striking his flesh
until his blood flowed to the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת פָּגַע בּוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after the death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא mourns רבי אליעזר with intense grief.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's eulogy for his teacher
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא eulogizes רבי אליעזר with a פסוק and a parable about coins with no money changer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He began a eulogy for him in the row of comforters and said: 'My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and its horsemen.' I have many coins, but I have no money changer to exchange them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא speaks a eulogy. He compares his many questions to coins that no one can now exchange.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'coins' are רבי עקיבא's questions in תורה. The 'money changer' is רבי אליעזר, who could have answered them. Now that he is gone, the questions have no one to answer them.

keyTerms.meaning: The row of people comforting the mourners

steps.whatToRemember: The story ends with רבי עקיבא's pain: he has many questions, and the great teacher who could answer them is gone.

phrases.english: He began a eulogy over him in the row and said:
My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and its horsemen.
I have many coins,
and I have no money changer to exchange them.
phrases.notes: The coins are his questions, and the money changer is רבי אליעזר, who could have answered them.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּתַח עָלָיו בְּשׁוּרָה וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the mourning scene.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא laments that no one is left to answer his questions.

steps.title: Did רבי עקיבא learn the cucumber magic from רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the story shows רבי עקיבא learned the cucumber magic from רבי אליעזר, but earlier he quoted it in the name of רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Apparently, he learned it from רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The story is over, and the גמרא goes back to its halachic discussion. It points out a contradiction about who taught רבי עקיבא the cucumber magic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא, רבי עקיבא taught the cucumber case in the name of רבי יהושע. But the story (step 12) shows that רבי אליעזר taught it to him. So which teacher did he learn it from?

phrases.english: Apparently,
he learned it from Rabbi Eliezer?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the cucumber magic. But earlier, רבי עקיבא taught it in רבי יהושע's name.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא, מֵרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר גַּמְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא and completes the challenge opened in step 1: the story shows רבי עקיבא learned the cucumber case from רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier teaching that רבי עקיבא learned the cucumber case from רבי יהושע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The story shows that רבי אליעזר taught him, which contradicts quoting it in רבי יהושע's name.

steps.title: He learned from both, but רבי יהושע explained it
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא first learned it from רבי אליעזר without understanding it. Later he learned it again from רבי יהושע, who explained it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learned it from רבי אליעזר but did not understand it. Then he learned it again from רבי יהושע, and he explained it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction: both teachers taught him. Since only רבי יהושע made it clear, רבי עקיבא quoted it in his name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hearing a teaching is not the same as understanding it. רבי עקיבא names רבי יהושע because רבי יהושע gave him the understanding.

phrases.english: He learned it from Rabbi Eliezer but did not understand it.
Then he learned it again from Rabbi Yehoshua,
and he explained it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּמְרַהּ מֵרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְלָא סַבְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: both sources are true at different stages.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is only one teacher, so the two accounts contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: He learned it from רבי אליעזר first and from רבי יהושע later. He quotes רבי יהושע, who explained it.

steps.title: How could רבי אליעזר perform magic?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the משנה says one who performs כישוף is liable, so how did רבי אליעזר do it?
steps.simpleTranslation: How could he do this? But we learned in the משנה: one who performs an act of כישוף is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second problem. Creating the cucumbers by magic seems to break the law of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה rules that a מכשף who performs a real act is liable. Filling the field with cucumbers was a real act, so how could a great צדיק like רבי אליעזר do it?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)?
One who performs an actual act (of כישוף)

phrases.english: How could he do this?
phrases.notes: He means רבי אליעזר filling the field with cucumbers by magic.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the mishna:
One who performs an act is liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי עָבֵיד הָכִי? וְהָאֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge on the same story, this time from our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's act of making cucumbers by magic.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes one who performs כישוף liable, so the act seems forbidden.

steps.title: Learning in order to understand and teach is permitted
steps.stepSummary: Doing magic in order to learn is different. The פסוק forbids learning it in order to practice, but allows learning it to understand and to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doing it to learn is different. As the Master said: 'Do not learn to do.' You may not learn in order to do, but you may learn in order to understand and to teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר did the act only to teach רבי עקיבא, and that is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'לא תלמד לעשות', which the גמרא reads as forbidding learning in order to practice. Learning it in order to understand and teach is permitted. רבי אליעזר's act was a teaching demonstration, not real practice.

keyTerms.meaning: To understand and to teach (to rule)

steps.whatToRemember: The prohibition of כישוף is about practicing it. Learning it, even with a demonstration, in order to understand and teach is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a lasting rule: forbidden practices may be studied for understanding and for ruling on הלכה, as long as one does not study them in order to use them.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי אליעזר's act was a real case of 'הָעוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשֶׂה'. It falls under the allowance of learning in order to teach.

phrases.english: To learn is different,
as the Master said:
"You shall not learn to do":
to do, you may not learn,
but you may learn to understand and to teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהִתְלַמֵּד שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on purpose (learning versus practicing).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any act of כישוף makes one liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Doing it in order to learn and teach is permitted, based on 'לא תלמד לעשות'.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing ארבע מיתות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally closes the פרק ארבע מיתות with the traditional הדרן formula.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter ארבע מיתות.
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק is over. This line is a closing formula that says goodbye to the chapter ארבע מיתות and promises we will come back to learn it again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new argument or ruling is added here. It is simply the end of the פרק, which has just finished with the discussion of whether כישוף may be learned for the sake of understanding and teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you": the traditional words said when finishing a פרק
"Four death penalties": the name of the seventh פרק of סנהדרין, taken from its opening words
A chapter of the משנה and גמרא

steps.whatToRemember: The פרק ארבע מיתות ends here. It covered the four death penalties of בית דין: סקילה, שריפה, הרג, and חנק. It closed with the laws of כישוף and the conclusion that one may learn it in order to understand and to teach.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a statement by any חכם and not part of the argument. It is just the standard closing line printed at the end of every פרק.

phrases.english: We will return to you, Four Death Penalties

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the perek right after the final answer about learning כישוף in order to understand and teach.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק ארבע מיתות is complete. The learner promises to return to it.
